key_insight: Coercivity-aware machine learning can efficiently narrow rare-earth-free soft magnetic alloy candidates by jointly screening Curie temperature and coercivity, with Fe-Co-rich compositions emerging as the most promising.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical computational workflow for accelerating magnetic alloy discovery while reducing costly experimental trial-and-error for transformer and motor material design.
method: Train ML models on compiled magnetic-material data using composition-grouped splits to avoid duplicate-composition leakage.
Compare elemental fractions vs. composition-weighted elemental descriptors for Curie-temperature and coercivity prediction.
Add uncertainty-aware screening using residual-based prediction intervals and distance-to-training filters, then validate selected Fe-Co systems with first-principles and atomistic spin simulations.
evidence_signal: Composition-grouped evaluation produced lower accuracy than random splits, showing that performance drops when predicting truly unseen compositions and that the uncertainty filters substantially shrink the candidate set.
watch_item: Coercivity is strongly influenced by processing and microstructure, so composition-only ML may not reliably predict it without manufacturing and microstructural features.
paper_title: Coercivity-Aware Machine Learning Discovery of Rare-Earth-Free Soft Magnetic Alloys with First-Principles Magnetic Benchmarks
